title: Repost your best short videos automatically with an agent
summary: A creator had Codex pull their reel analytics in Chrome, ask Claude Code to review its build, and set up automatic reposting of top videos as trial reels.
agent_role: Codex opened Chrome to fetch analytics, built the reposting system and launched Claude Code for review; the human directed it from their phone.
outcome: Author says the system will push out his best-performing videos as trial reels automatically.
what_they_did: A creator let Codex run freely on his computer while he steered from his phone. Codex opened Chrome and fetched full analytics for his reels. It built a system to repost top videos as trial reels, scheduled with his own tool. Then it launched Claude Code to review the build.
how_it_went: The author says the system will now push out his best-performing videos as trial reels automatically. He shares no numbers yet.
worth_knowing: He gives Codex free rein over his whole computer, including the browser, which carries real risk to accounts.
prompt: Open my [video platform] analytics in the browser and list my top [10] short videos by views and engagement from the last [30 days]. Then draft a plan to repost the best ones as trial posts on a schedule using [my scheduling tool]. Ask a second agent to review the plan for problems. Show me the list, the schedule and the review, and wait for my approval before posting or scheduling anything.

curation.rationale: A genuine multi-step agent workflow (browser analytics, second-agent review, scheduled reposting), but lightly evidenced and ends in a course plug.
